rules.title: FEHA housing discrimination ban including source of income
rules.requirement: Owners of housing may not discriminate against or harass any person because of protected characteristics, including source of income (e.g., Section 8 and other housing vouchers or public assistance). Owners also may not ask applicants about most protected characteristics or publish ads indicating a preference based on them.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of any housing accommodation in California, and persons advertising or publishing notices about rentals.
rules.exemptions: Inquiries about the level or source of income are not source-of-income discrimination. A landlord is not a tenant's representative unless the income is a HUD-VASH voucher.
rules.quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.conflict_note: The document shows only the most recent amendment (Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, SB 267, effective January 1, 2024). It does not give the original effective date of the source-of-income protection, so effective_date is left null. The provision is in force as of the query date.

rules.title: Credit history use for subsidized applicants requires alternative-evidence option (SB 267)
rules.requirement: Where a government rent subsidy is involved, a housing provider may not use an applicant's credit history unless it offers the applicant the option of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion of rent, such as benefit payments, pay records, or bank statements. If the applicant chooses this option, the provider must give reasonable time to respond and must reasonably consider that evidence instead of credit history.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental applications where there is a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Owners may still verify employment, request landlord references, and verify identity.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where there is a government rent subsidy.

rules.quoted_span: (B) (i) Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
rules.conflict_note: The effective date comes from the amendment note (SB 267, Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, effective January 1, 2024), which is presumed to have added this credit-history provision.

rules.title: Income standard for subsidized tenants must be based on the tenant's portion of rent
rules.requirement: Where there is a government rent subsidy, a landlord may not apply an income or financial eligibility standard based on anything other than the portion of rent the tenant pays.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing eligibility assessments where there is a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Owners may still verify employment, request landlord references, and verify identity.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where there is a government rent subsidy.

rules.quoted_span: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.conflict_note: The document shows only the latest amendment (effective January 1, 2024) and not the original effective date of this subdivision.

rules.title: Income standards must count the aggregate income of co-residents
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use an income standard that fails to count the combined income of people living or proposing to live together on the same basis as married persons' combined income.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental of housing accommodations in California.
rules.quoted_span: (n) To use a financial or income standard in the rental of housing that fails to account for the aggregate income of persons residing together or proposing to reside together on the same basis as the aggregate income
rules.conflict_note: The document does not state the original effective date for this subdivision.
